key_insight: A proposed cognitive framework maps four ways LLMs can approximate learning by thinking while linking their failure modes to structural differences from human cognition.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers design hypotheses for more reliable autonomous learning systems by distinguishing inference-time gains from durable parameter learning.
method: Map reflective reasoning, synthetic memory formation, internal simulation, and conceptual self-organization onto LLM processes.
Analyze representative methods, including chain-of-thought, self-reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts, and Self-Instruct.
Connect characteristic failures to four structural asymmetries between LLMs and human cognition.
evidence_signal: As a cited example rather than a new experiment, Self-Instruct generated approximately 52,000 instructions from 175 seed tasks and reported a 33-percentage-point improvement on Super-NaturalInstructions.
watch_item: Closed, ungrounded self-learning loops can propagate hallucinations or model collapse, and improved task performance need not imply durable learning.
paper_title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
